canonical.title: The utility belt: per-tool Linux verdicts for a Windows power user (2026)

parent.title: Throwing away Windows: a replacement plan for an actual installed-software inventory

siblings.title: Your .NET + SQL Server stack on Linux: what actually replaces what
siblings.summary: Rider replaces Visual Studio + ReSharper on Linux at the cost of the WinForms/WPF designers; SQL Server itself moves cleanly to a container, but SSMS has no Linux successor now that Azure Data Studio is dead.

siblings.title: Microsoft 365 on Linux in 2026: what you actually lose
siblings.summary: Office, Teams and mail are a tolerable compromise on Linux in 2026; OneDrive sync and OneNote are the two places where the gap is real.

siblings.title: Multi-monitor, window management and the desktop shell: replacing DisplayFusion, Fences, FancyZones and X-Rite on Linux
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma 6.7 is the only Linux desktop that replaces most of DisplayFusion and FancyZones natively; Fences has no real equivalent and the X-Rite workflow becomes ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL plus a per-screen ICC profile.

siblings.title: Gaming after the switch: your library survives, the NVIDIA App does not
siblings.summary: Both installed games run under Proton — Planetfall is Gold/Deck-Playable and Fall Guys' EAC is Linux-enabled — so the only hard loss is the NVIDIA App and Game Bar tooling layer, which becomes environment variables plus MangoHud and GPU Screen Recorder.

siblings.title: Legion hardware, peripherals and the two corporate VPNs on Linux
siblings.summary: Neither corporate VPN blocks the switch — Harmony SASE ships an official Linux agent and WatchGuard is reachable with plain OpenVPN; the real losses are QuantumENGINE, Dolby, XTU and Lenovo's AI/Space bloat.

siblings.title: Escape hatches for the leftovers: Wine, a VM, passthrough, or just keep the partition
siblings.summary: Wine for single-window utilities, a local Windows VM for Visual Studio and SSMS, RDP for the corporate cluster — and no GPU passthrough on a muxless Legion.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — PowerToys utilities
sources.claim: Complete list of PowerToys utilities shipping as of 2026, used to break PowerToys down per module.

sources.title: Lemmy — AutoHotkey alternatives on Linux
sources.claim: Community consensus in 2026 is that no single Linux tool replaces AutoHotkey; users must combine several, and window automation is DE/WM-specific.

sources.title: keyd
sources.claim: keyd remaps at the evdev/uinput kernel layer and is therefore display-server agnostic, working under X11, Wayland and bare VTs.

sources.title: kanata — platform known issues
sources.claim: kanata's documented Linux limitations: unicode output depends on ibus, and rapid key events can misfire.

sources.title: keymapper
sources.claim: keymapper is the closest structural analogue to AutoHotkey's per-application context rules, but on Wayland the compositor must feed it focus information.

sources.title: Espanso — Linux install docs
sources.claim: Espanso ships separate X11 and Wayland builds; Wayland support is experimental, needs setcap, and has documented limitations.

sources.title: AutoKey issue #1061 — Wayland
sources.claim: Upstream AutoKey is an Xorg application and does not function in a Wayland session.

sources.title: autokey-wayland fork
sources.claim: The autokey-wayland fork is the only AutoKey that runs under Wayland, and only on GNOME (KDE support planned).

sources.title: ydotool
sources.claim: ydotool synthesises input through the kernel uinput framework instead of X events, so it works on Wayland, but its daemon needs root-level access to /dev/uinput.

sources.title: who-t — libei integrations in XDG RemoteDesktop
sources.claim: libei is integrated into the XDG RemoteDesktop and InputCapture portals since portal 1.17, with session persistence since 1.21.

sources.title: Wayland GlobalShortcuts portal learnings
sources.claim: GlobalShortcuts portal coverage is uneven in 2026: wlroots-based compositors ship no implementation at all, so BindShortcuts fails.

sources.title: The Register — GNOME 50 is Wayland-only
sources.claim: GNOME 50 (March 2026) removed the X11 session entirely; X11 apps only run via XWayland.

sources.title: 9to5Linux — Plasma 6.8 drops the X11 session
sources.claim: KDE Plasma 6.8, due October 2026, drops the X11 session and goes Wayland-only.

sources.title: Flameshot — Wayland help
sources.claim: Flameshot's own docs document Wayland breakage — repeated portal permission prompts on GNOME, multi-monitor overlay problems, and shortcuts that fail to trigger.

sources.title: CopyQ — known issues
sources.claim: CopyQ works on Wayland with caveats: global shortcuts need xdg-desktop-portal, GNOME needs a Shell extension, and modifier/mouse-position queries do not work.

sources.title: QDirStat issue #97 — disk usage tools compared
sources.claim: Comparison of Linux disk-usage analysers establishing QDirStat as the closest WinDirStat analogue.

sources.title: 7-Zip downloads
sources.claim: 7-Zip ships an official Linux console build (version 26.02, 2026-06-25) for x86-64, x86, arm64 and arm.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn — install Power Automate for desktop
sources.claim: Power Automate for desktop installs only via a Windows MSI or the Microsoft Store and depends on the Windows Desktop .NET runtime.

sources.title: opensource.com — edit PDFs on Linux with pdftk
sources.claim: pdftk-java is a maintained Java port of PDFtk that keeps the same command-line interface on Linux.

sources.title: 1Password — install on Linux
sources.claim: The 1Password Flatpak build loses system authentication, the SSH agent, and unified app/browser unlock.

sources.title: 1Password — system authentication on Linux
sources.claim: 1Password on Linux can be unlocked with the Linux user password, fingerprint or other biometrics, or a security key.

sources.title: It's FOSS — Notepad++ alternatives for Linux
sources.claim: Notepad++ has no official Linux build; the Wine/Snap route is an unofficial third-party effort.

sources.title: RustDesk for Linux
sources.claim: RustDesk captures the screen on Wayland via PipeWire and the XDG desktop portal, supports multi-monitor since 1.4.3, and a permanent password for unattended access.

sources.title: How-To Geek — forget Phone Link, use KDE Connect
sources.claim: KDE Connect exceeds Phone Link on features over LAN with no cloud account.

sources.title: Linux sandboxing tools compared
sources.claim: Firejail is the lowest-friction Sandboxie analogue for distro-packaged apps; bubblewrap ships no ready-made profiles; Flatpak only confines Flatpak-installed apps.

sources.title: AlternativeTo — IrfanView on Linux
sources.claim: The crowd-ranked Linux replacements for IrfanView are XnView MP (closest, closed-source), then nomacs, gThumb, qView, Gwenview and qimgv.

sources.title: AlternativeTo — Paint.NET on Linux
sources.claim: Pinta is the crowd-ranked closest free/open replacement for Paint.NET on Linux.

sources.title: How-To Geek — Linux alternatives for PowerToys
sources.claim: Per-module PowerToys mappings on Linux: Albert for PowerToys Run, NormCap for Text Extractor, gpick/KColorChooser for Color Picker.

sources.title: Linux Today — alternatives to Clipchamp
sources.claim: Kdenlive, Shotcut and OpenShot are the free/open Linux replacements for Clipchamp.

sources.title: LinuxSecurity — what is ClamAV
sources.claim: ClamAV is a signature scanner, not an EDR: no behavioural analysis, memory scanning or automated response.

sources.title: UI.Vision RPA
sources.claim: UI.Vision RPA is a cross-platform (Linux included) open-source RPA tool running locally.

sources.title: Sandboxie-Plus
sources.claim: Sandboxie-Plus is a Windows-only sandbox built on Windows kernel drivers; there is no Linux port.
